proof_summary: For composite \(n\), an odd prime divisor \(p\) is shown—using Fermat factors and Legendre’s digit-sum formula—to divide \(a(n-1)\), forcing the impossible \(p\mid 2^{n-2}\); if \(n=2^k\), the exact valuation \(v_2(a(2^k-1))=k-1\) gives the analogous contradiction. Once \(n\) is prime, any proper order \(d<n-1\) of \(2\) makes the factor \(2^d-1\) force \(n\mid a(n-1)\) (uncancelled by \((n-1)!\)), again impossibly implying \(n\mid 2^{n-2}\).
